review.tagline: Plugin that builds an explorable knowledge graph of a codebase or wiki
review.summary: Understand Anything is a plugin for Claude Code and about 15 other agent platforms. Its /understand command runs a multi-agent pipeline that combines Tree-sitter parsing with LLM summaries to write a knowledge graph to .ua/knowledge-graph.json. A local dashboard then offers graph navigation, search, guided tours, diff impact analysis and chat, and /understand-knowledge handles Karpathy-style LLM wikis.
review.audience: Engineers onboarding to large codebases or LLM wikis using AI coding agents
strengths: Tree-sitter extracts imports and call sites deterministically, so structural edges are reproducible
Graph is plain JSON that can be committed; teammates view it with Node.js >= 18 and no LLM
Incremental re-analysis of changed files, plus an optional post-commit auto-update hook
Installs on Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Kiro and others
weaknesses: First /understand run on a large repo can use a significant number of tokens
Needs a host agent platform and an LLM; it is not a standalone tool
Output languages limited to en, zh, zh-TW, ja, ko, ru, vi
Graphs over 10 MB need git-lfs to commit comfortably
needs: Needs Claude Code or another supported agent platform, Node.js >= 18 (standalone viewer), pnpm (building from source)
Models: Whatever the host platform uses, Local models via Ollama
